MTDI for AI assistants

You were given this repository and asked to use MTDI for a project. This page is the procedure. Follow it in order; do not summarise MTDI from memory and stop there.

What MTDI is, in one paragraph

MTDI (Microprocessing Technological Diagnostic Intelligence) turns anything that produces numbers into channels, and runs five pillars over them: 00 Validation Chamber (is each channel present, fresh, on time, in range), 01 Environmental Intelligence (learn the normal environment, lock it, compare against it), 02 NVTRA (explain what is happening, in plain language, from evidence only), 03 I³ (the interface), and 04 Aether (purpose and authorship, never scored). A core fuses 00 and 01 into one score of eight named factors that can be taken apart. It is pure Python, small enough for a Raspberry Pi, and driven entirely by one project.json per project.

Step 0: read, don't guess

Read these files before writing anything, in this order:

  1. README.md
  2. INTEGRATING.md, the integration procedure
  3. docs/MANIFEST.md, every manifest field (machine-readable: docs/schema/project.schema.json)
  4. firmware/PROTOCOL.md, the line format firmware and probes print
  5. One worked example close to the user's field:
FieldExample
Sensors, embedded, physicsprojects/inductra-vaion, projects/ultrasonic-room
Computers, single-board computers, DevOpsprojects/host-health
Networkingprojects/network-watch
Cybersecurityprojects/auth-watch

python -m mtdi describe prints every adapter, domain, block kind and rule operator as JSON.

Step 1: choose the mode

  • The project lives in this repository: python -m mtdi new <id> creates projects/<id>.
  • The project has its own repository: python -m mtdi adopt <path-to-that-repo> copies MTDI into it (mtdi/), creates mtdi-project/project.json, and adds MTDI rules to its AGENTS.md. Prefer this when the user says "use MTDI in my project".

Step 2: map the project to channels

Make a table with the user before writing the manifest. One row per quantity:

What is measuredWhere it comes fromAdapterKeysUnitDomain

How each field becomes channels:

FieldTypical channelsTypical adapter
Hardware / sensorsfield strength, distance, temperature, acceleration, currentserial (firmware prints protocol lines), tcp
Firmwareloop time, free memory, reset count, error countersserial (add them to the same lines)
Softwarelatency, error rate, queue depth, request rate, build timeprocess (a probe script), python, http
Computer / SBCCPU, memory, load, temperature, disk, networksystem (built in)
NetworkingRTT, packet loss, throughput, DNS timeprocess probe
Cybersecurityfailed logins, new connections, firewall drops, privilege escalationsprocess probe reading logs
Data / scienceany instrument or dataset with a timestamped numberreplay, python

Write the table down. Ask the user for anything you cannot read from their code or datasheets.

Step 3: write the sources

  • Firmware: start from firmware/mtdi_template_arduino or firmware/mtdi_template_micropython. If firmware already prints KEY=value lines, keep it and map its keys.
  • Software: write a probe that prints KEY=value lines to stdout and declare it with the process adapter, as in projects/network-watch/probe.py.
  • On failure, print nothing. Never print a stand-in value.

Step 4: write project.json

Start from projects/_template/project.json. Set noise_floor from the datasheet or a measurement; if unknown, keep the default and write "unknown, to be set from the measured LOD" in the project README. Add simulate blocks so the project runs before the hardware exists. Add NVTRA rules for the field's own knowledge. Each rule's text must say what the pattern suggests and what else could cause it.

Step 5: verify, then report honestly

python -m mtdi check <project>
python -m mtdi run <project> --simulate      # every page renders, every pillar responds
python -m mtdi packet <project> --simulate --seconds 15
python -m unittest discover tests            # when working inside MTDI Studio

Report what was verified and what was not (for example "firmware not run on hardware").

Non-negotiable rules

  1. Projects are manifests. Never put project-specific code in mtdi/.
  2. Never invent readings, calibrations, noise floors or results.
  3. Simulated data is labelled SIMULATED end to end. Never remove the label.
  4. Never edit another repository the user did not ask you to change.
  5. MTDI's score is a heuristic evidence-quality score, not a probability. Say so.
  6. Manifests can start programs (process adapter). Only run manifests you wrote or the user trusts.
